atAGlance: Bò bía is thin fresh rolls with jicama and sausage, usually with egg, herbs, dried shrimp, and peanut-hoisin sauce.
whatItIs: Bò bía is a soft rice-paper roll with jicama, Chinese sausage, egg, dried shrimp, herbs, and peanut-hoisin dip. It is sweet, savory, crunchy, and snacky.
howToEnjoy: Dip each roll in peanut-hoisin and eat while the rice paper is still soft. Ask about peanuts or dried shrimp if allergies matter.
howLocalsOrder: Order bò bía as a snack by the roll or plate. Ask for no peanuts or no dried shrimp before the roll is made.
worthKnowing: At Vietnamese snack stalls, bò bía is not a beef roll; the usual flavor comes from jicama, sausage, egg, herbs, and peanut-hoisin dip.
goodToKnow: If peanut-hoisin dip or nước chấm, a lime-fish-sauce dip comes separately, start with a small dip; it can be salty, sweet, sour, and spicy at once.
